basis: The founder's personal position, decisions.md D2: Facebook's 2012 registration statement lists the holder as Hommels Holding GmbH, his private company, and no Lakestar entity appears in any Facebook filing. The firm shows the logo on its 2018-2019 and 2026 homepages, never on its 2022-2026 portfolio page, and says its platform 'spans institutional venture capital funds and personal investments'.

The founder's personal position, decisions.md D2: Klaus Hommels invested in Skype as a private investor ('when I invested in Skype ... it was so early', his 2015 interview) and was out by Microsoft's purchase in 2011, before Lakestar existed. Logo on the 2018-2019 homepage only.

The founder's personal position, decisions.md D2: 'While the company talks up its investments in major firms such as Airbnb and Spotify, these came about because of Hommels' early, personal bets' (Business Insider, 2019-06); no Lakestar or Hommels entity is in Airbnb's 2020 registration statement and no round names a Lakestar fund. Logo on the 2018-2019 and 2026 homepages, never on the 2022-2026 portfolio page.

The founder's personal position, decisions.md D2: the press attributes Klarna to Klaus Hommels himself (New York Times, 2015-08-24); no round announcement and no filing (Klarna's 2025 registration statement) names a Lakestar vehicle. Logo on the 2018-2019 and 2026 homepages, never on the 2022-2026 portfolio page.

The founder's personal position, decisions.md D2: King's 2014 registration statement names 'Klaus Hommels, a former member of our board of directors, and certain entities affiliated with Mr. Hommels' as holders whose shares the company repurchased by 23 June 2011, before Lakestar existed. Logo on the 2018-2019 homepage only.

The founder's personal position, decisions.md D2: the only source attributes Coinbase to Klaus Hommels himself (Forbes profile); no round announcement and no filing (Coinbase's registration statement) names a Lakestar vehicle. Logo on the 2026 homepage only, never on the 2022-2026 portfolio page.

The founder's personal position, decisions.md D2: SumUp's $20M Series A of August 2012 names 'Klaus Hommels' as an investor beside b-to-v, Shortcut and Tengelmann (TechCrunch, 2012-08-23), and no later round names Lakestar. Listed on the 2013 site and the 2026 homepage, never on the 2022-2026 portfolio page.

Not shown to be a fund position, decisions.md D2: no Helsing round (2021 seed, Series B 2023, C 2024, D 2025, E 2026) names Lakestar among its investors, and the trade press calls Klaus Hommels 'an angel investor' in Helsing (Tech Funding News, 2025). The firm names Helsing in its Resilience portfolio (2026) but never listed it on its 2022-2026 portfolio page, and says its platform includes personal investments. Out until a round or filing names a Lakestar fund; raised at close as an open ruling.
